content: The World Health Organization (WHO) provides several recommendations for the use of digital interventions to strengthen health systems. These recommendations are as follows: 1. Digital Death Notification: WHO recommends the use of digital death notification systems under specific conditions. These include settings where rigorous research is conducted, where the notifications provide individual-level data to the health system or civil registration and vital statistics (CRVS) systems, and where these systems have the capacity to respond to the notifications. The health system must be able to accept the notifications and trigger appropriate health and social services, while the CRVS system must validate the information to initiate the processes of death registration and certification. 2. Digital Stock Notification and Commodity Management: WHO recommends the use of digital systems for stock notification and commodity management in settings where supply chain management systems can respond promptly and appropriately to stock notifications. 3. Client-to-Provider Telemedicine: WHO supports the use of client-to-provider telemedicine to complement, rather than replace, traditional health service delivery. This is recommended in settings where patient safety, privacy, traceability, accountability, and security can be monitored. Monitoring should include protocols for patient consent, data protection and storage, and verification of provider licensing and credentials. 4. Provider-to-Provider Telemedicine: This requires the establishment of standard operating procedures to address patient consent, data protection, and verification of provider credentials. 5. Targeted Client Communication: WHO recommends the use of digital targeted client communication for health issues related to sexual, reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health. This is contingent on addressing concerns about sensitive content and data privacy. 6. Digital Decision Support for Health Workers: WHO recommends the use of digital decision support tools accessible via mobile devices for community and facility-based health workers. These tools should be used for tasks already defined within the health worker’s scope of practice. 7. Digital Tracking of Clients’ Health Status and Services: WHO supports the use of digital tracking systems combined with decision support in settings where the health system can implement these components in an integrated manner. These systems should be used for tasks within the health worker’s defined scope of practice. 8. Digital Tracking Combined with Decision Support and Targeted Client Communication: WHO recommends the use of digital tracking systems that integrate decision support and targeted client communication. This is recommended in settings where the health system can support integrated implementation, where tasks are within the health worker’s scope of practice, and where concerns about data privacy and sensitive content can be addressed. 9. Digital Provision of Educational and Training Content for Health Workers: WHO recommends the use of digital platforms to provide educational and training content to health workers. This should complement, rather than replace, traditional methods of delivering continued health education and post-certification training. These recommendations aim to address various health system needs in interconnected ways. Health workers benefit from tools like decision support and digital learning platforms to deliver high-quality care. Collectively, these digital interventions contribute to strengthening health systems and advancing universal health coverage (UHC).
